caption: The drawing features a single ornate teapot rendered in shades of gray and black, suggesting a metallic surface, possibly silver or pewter. The teapot stands on a wide, circular base with fluted decorative elements extending upward to a broad, bulbous body adorned with floral and foliate engravings. At the center of the body, within an inscribed oval framed by additional floral motifs, there is text that reads "Lee and James from their Papa Christmas 1861.” The teapot’s neck is encircled by a band of round floral medallions, leading up to a tall, pointed domed lid capped with a finial and further decorated with intricate patterns. To the left, an elaborate, curving handle is embellished with round knobs along its outer edge and a hinge at its base. On the right, a long, curved spout features similar round knobs along its spine, and the spout ends in a hooked tip. The overall composition is centered on a plain, light beige background, and the artist’s signature, "Eugene Croe," appears in the lower right corner.
title: Silver Teapot
